steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AVQ-Attention-2: Adaptive Vector-Quantized Attention with Exact Local Blocks and Linear-Cost Training
summary: It replaces exact quadratic attention in pretrained transformers with an approximate layer that clusters keys, attends to exact local blocks plus per-cluster key means, and can be dropped in without fine-tuning. Costs include O(NM) compute in both training and inference, the added complexity of codebook maintenance and cluster-assignment logic, and a custom kernel implementation outside the standard FlashAttention stack. Failure modes include quality degradation on workloads where attention mass does not concentrate in few clusters, approximation error accumulating across layers, and integration risk if no maintained implementation exists for the reader's inference framework.
rationale: The technique targets exactly the long-context attention bottleneck that constrained-infrastructure teams face, but as a new approximate-attention method it requires validation against FlashAttention baselines on the reader's actual sequence lengths and models before production adoption.
technique: Adaptive vector-quantized attention with local blocks

claims.statement: It replaces exact quadratic attention in pretrained transformers with an approximate layer that clusters keys, attends to exact local blocks plus per-cluster key means, and can be dropped in without fine-tuning. Costs include O(NM) compute in both training and inference, the added complexity of codebook maintenance and cluster-assignment logic, and a custom kernel implementation outside the standard FlashAttention stack. Failure modes include quality degradation on workloads where attention mass does not concentrate in few clusters, approximation error accumulating across layers, and integration risk if no maintained implementation exists for the reader's inference framework.

Competitive with exact dense attention in quality while running faster than FlashAttention across a variety of sequence lengths, with O(NM) training cost instead of O(N^2); no numeric speedup factor is stated in the abstract.
